method: Read from the release file by Claude Opus 5.5: the agent's run_command tool, its confirmation rule (getRunCommandConfirmationReason) and the command patterns it checks.
label: Its AI agent can run commands on your computer; it asks only for ones that look destructive
summary: In agent mode the AI can run shell commands as you. It asks you first only when a command looks destructive (deleting, moving, installing, changing permissions or git history), pipes a download into a shell, automates other apps or system settings, or overwrites an existing file. Anything else runs without asking, including commands that read your files, run scripts or send data over the network.

facts.confirmationRule: run_command.shouldRequireConfirmation returns true only when getRunCommandConfirmationReason matches NETWORK_TO_SHELL_PATTERN, SYSTEM_AUTOMATION_PATTERN, DESTRUCTIVE_COMMANDS, an appending redirect, or a write to a path that already exists.
facts.destructivePattern: rm, rmdir, mv, rename, chmod, chown, sudo, mkfs, dd; npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/brew/apt/conda/cargo/gem installs; git init/add/commit/push/reset/checkout/clean/rebase and similar; setting the date or time.
facts.notCovered: curl or wget without a pipe into a shell, cat, python or node scripts, and any other program not in the patterns run without a prompt.
facts.settings: No setting changes this; there are no permission modes.
